Your questions

A little clarity.

The essentials, before you begin.

What is the Amber approach?+
Amber brings together defined infusion formulations and structured programmes. A clinician assesses your needs, considers whether an infusion is appropriate, and guides your care under medical supervision.
How do I choose an infusion?+
Start with a consultation. Your clinician will review your health history and individual needs before recommending an option. The collection is here to help you understand the range and prepare questions for that conversation.
What is the difference between a kit and a programme?+
A kit contains the components for one session. A programme is a prescribed course of sessions over several weeks, with the appropriate kit chosen for each session.
How long should I allow for a session?+
Infusion time is typically around 60–90 minutes, depending on the prescribed formulation. Allow additional time for your consultation and preparation, and confirm the total visit time with your clinician.
Do I need a consultation first?+
Yes. Amber infusions require a clinician’s assessment and prescription. Your medical history, current medicines and individual suitability are considered before treatment.
What should I discuss with my clinician?+
Share your health history, current medicines and supplements, any allergies, and any pregnancy or breastfeeding considerations. Ask about suitability, possible risks, alternatives and what to expect from your session.
